# Mergeway CLI

Mergeway CLI manages structured metadata in Git-backed workspaces. It defines entity schemas in YAML or JSON Schema, loads YAML/JSON records from disk, validates schema and reference integrity, formats files deterministically, diffs logical data changes, and exports snapshots.

## LLM Quick Context

- The workspace root contains `mergeway.yaml`.
- Config files can `include` other YAML files that add more `entities`.
- Each entity must declare exactly one of `fields` or `json_schema`.
- References are expressed by setting `type` to another entity name, for example `author: User`. There is no native `type: ref`.
- Arrays use `repeated: true`. There is no native `list[...]` field syntax.
- Native nested objects use `type: object` plus `properties`. Do not nest `fields:` inside a field.
- Reference unions such as `User | Team` are supported only in native `fields:` definitions. They are not supported in `json_schema` entities and cannot be exported with `config export`.
- `identifier` can be a field name (`id`), a mapping (`field`, optional `generated`, optional `pattern`), or the reserved `$path`.
- `identifier: $path` means the workspace-relative file path is the object ID. It only works for one-object-per-file sources and cannot be combined with inline `data`.
- Records can come from inline `data`, globbed files in `include`, or `include` mappings with `path` plus JSONPath `selector`.
- Selector-backed records and external-root `$path` records are readable, validatable, and exportable, but not writable via `create`, `update`, or `delete`.
- `mergeway-cli validate` exits non-zero when errors are found.

## Canonical Native Schema Pattern

```yaml
mergeway:
  version: 1

entities:
  Post:
    description: Blog posts
    identifier: id
    include:
      - data/posts/*.yaml
    fields:
      id:
        type: string
        required: true
      title:
        type: string
        required: true
      author:
        type: User
        required: true
      status:
        type: enum
        enum: [DRAFT, PUBLISHED]
        required: true
      metadata:
        type: object
        properties:
          created_at:
            type: string
          editor:
            type: User
      contacts:
        type: object
        repeated: true
        properties:
          label:
            type: string
            required: true
          email:
            type: string
            format: email
```

Important details:

- Native nested object fields must use `properties`.
- Repeated arrays are modeled with `repeated: true` on the same field definition.
- Native enums use `type: enum` plus an `enum:` list.
- Type names must start with an uppercase letter. Field/property names use letters, digits, `_`, and `-`.

## Useful Field Attributes

- `required`: field must be present unless a `default` is defined.
- `repeated`: field value must be an array.
- `description`: human-readable context.
- `enum`: allowed values when `type: enum`.
- `default`: used when the field is missing during validation; it is not automatically written back to source files.
- `unique`: field value must be unique across objects of the same entity. Not allowed together with `repeated: true`.
- `pattern`: regex constraint for identifier fields and string-like fields.
- `format`: runtime validation currently recognizes `email`, `uri`, and `url`.

## Command Surface

- `init`: scaffold a workspace.
- `entity list`, `entity show`: inspect discovered entities and normalized schema.
- `list`, `get`, `create`, `update`, `delete`: work with records.
- `diff`: compare Mergeway-managed data between snapshots; config changes are excluded.
- `export`: emit a combined YAML/JSON snapshot.
- `fmt`: canonicalize file ordering and formatting.
- `validate`: run format, schema, and reference validation phases.
- `config lint`: validate config only.
- `config export --type <Type>`: emit JSON Schema for a native Mergeway entity.
- `gen-erd --path <file>`: generate an ERD with Graphviz.
- `version`: print build metadata.

Global flags: `--root`, `--config`, `--format`, `--fail-fast`, `--yes`, `--verbose`.
